title: Detection of LVAD Driveline Infections by Thermal Imaging – an Observational Study
summary:
People with severe heart failure can receive a heart pump (LVAD). The pump is placed inside the body and connected by a cable, called the driveline, to a controller and batteries outside the body. The cable permanently passes through the skin of the abdomen. Bacteria can enter at this exit site and cause an infection. Such infections are dangerous, often hard to recognise and can lead to hospital stays or surgery. Patients therefore need regular check-ups at the outpatient clinic, often involving long journeys.

Inflamed skin is usually slightly warmer than healthy skin. A small thermal camera attached to a smartphone can measure this without contact, without pain and without radiation. In this study, we take a thermal image of the exit site at two regular check-ups. We want to find out whether a driveline infection can be reliably detected this way. In the long term, such an examination might also become possible remotely. Participants undergo no additional procedures and face no risks.
conditions: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to other cardiac and vascular devices, implants and grafts

interventions.name: Patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) followed up at the LVAD outpatient clinic of Klinikum Oldenburg. At two consecutive routine follow-up visits, the driveline exit site is imaged contactlessly and in a standardised way using a smartphone-based thermal camera (Hikmicro Mini2). Infl
